implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner is purchaser, staging technician, and payer, so duties cannot be separated. The contract bookkeeper does the monthly reconciliation and year-end tax preparation through a named, read-only accountant user in SYS-01. A first payment to a new account, or any change of bank details, is confirmed by a call to a number already on file, and marketplace sellers are paid only through the marketplace (POL-01 6.5). The bank enforces MFA. Gap: on 2026-05-19, before the call-back rule, a $2,340 broker invoice was paid to a fraudulent account.
evidence: SYS-01 user roles; monthly reconciliation; POL-01 6.5

implementation_statement: No rule limits which outside systems may hold business data or FCI. FCI was pasted into a consumer AI assistant (SYS-10) and shared through open file links. POL-01 section 8 sets approved locations; the AI assistant is limited by P10 by 2026-09-30.

Only the owner posts to the business website and social media page. Gap: a 2026-04 photo of a staged DoD pallet showed asset tags and building delivery labels; removed 2026-08-04. POL-01 9.4 now requires a check before posting anything about the prime's work.

The owner has only OEM partner sales training. The owner will complete a short security awareness course and a free anti-counterfeit and supply chain course, and review phishing and payment fraud examples each quarter, starting by 2026-11-30.

Compensating control (one-person business): the owner is the only administrator, so the audit records relied on are the sign-in histories that the SYS-01 vendor and the email provider keep, not files the owner keeps. The owner reviews them on the first business day of each month (POL-01 7.8).
evidence: SYS-01 and email sign-in history; vendor SOC 2 report (P09); POL-01 7.8

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner designed, operates, and assessed the controls, and P07 states that independence is limited. The on-call IT consultant ran the tests with the owner and challenged each answer, though the consultant also supports the laptop and router. POL-01 4.5 has the IT consultant check the evidence on screen at every annual CMMC Level 1 self-assessment. The accounting SaaS vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report (P09) covers inherited controls. Base CA-2 is the annual self-assessment.

Compensating control (one-person business): there is no change board and the business develops no software. SaaS changes are the vendors'. Under CM-3(g) the change control element for the owner's own setting changes (router, laptop) is the security log, where they are recorded (P09 CC8.1). Gap: there is no settings record for the router and laptop yet; it is due 2026-10-15 (POAM-007).

The accounting SaaS vendor backs up SYS-01 daily (RPO 24 hours in its SOC 2 system description). Owner responsibility: the laptop and the cloud file storage have no backup beyond the provider's recycle bin, and the serial-to-tag spreadsheets are often saved only on the laptop.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; laptop and file storage settings

implementation_statement: Each person has a unique account in each service (the owner; the bookkeeper in SYS-01). No shared accounts. Integrations (bank feed, payment page) run under the owner's authorization and are listed in the SYS-01 connections page.

implementation_statement: The bank enforces MFA. Email administrator sign-in uses SMS codes. Gap: the owner's SYS-01 administrator account signs in with a password only; MFA is available and free. Owner turns it on by 2026-09-15.
Distributor portal A enforces MFA. Email uses SMS codes, which are weaker than an authenticator app. Gap: distributor portal B offers no MFA, and the bookkeeper's SYS-01 account has no MFA.
SaaS services enforce minimum password rules. Gap: one password is reused across 4 services, there is no password manager, and the home router kept its default admin password until 2026-08-06 (P07).

The counterfeit and tampered product runbook (P08) with a contact list was adopted on 2026-08-31. It covers the FAR 52.204-25(d) and 52.204-23(c) report clocks. Gap: not yet walked through with the IT consultant (due 2026-09-30).

Paper tag sheets are cross-cut shredded at home. Gap: no wipe method or record for laptops, phones, or returned network equipment. The old phone was traded in during 2026-02 with no recorded wipe; 2 old laptops sit in a drawer unwiped; 2 trade-in switches in stock held customer configurations.

The garage door is kept closed and locked, and staged DoD equipment is kept in the locked steel cabinet. Gap: household members can enter the garage, the cabinet key hangs on the house key hook, and the garage keypad code (also known to a dog walker) has never changed. No log of drivers or customers who enter.
First risk assessment completed 2026-08-07 with NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed every August with the CMMC Level 1 self-assessment and after major changes.

The accounting SaaS vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report was reviewed on 2026-08-05 (P09). The IT consultant signed a confidentiality agreement on 2026-07-30 and works only in owner-watched sessions. Gap: no vendor list, and the AI assistant's consumer terms allow training on chats.

The ISP router's firewall blocks unsolicited inbound traffic, and the laptop host firewall is on. Gap: household devices share one flat network with the laptop; the router's default admin password and internet remote management were found and fixed on 2026-08-06; firmware is about 2 years old. A business-only Wi-Fi network is planned by 2026-10-15.

The laptop uses the operating system's built-in full-disk encryption (recovery key kept offline); the phone is encrypted by its passcode. SaaS vendors encrypt stored data (SYS-01 confirmed in its SOC 2 report).
evidence: Device encryption status; vendor SOC 2 report

implementation_statement: Automatic operating system and browser updates on the laptop and phone. Firmware for staged DoD devices is the version the prime specifies, tested on the bench switch first. Gap: router firmware about 2 years old; no written approach for when updates are tested.
The built-in antivirus runs real-time and daily scheduled scans with automatic signature updates. Owner responsibility: keep it on and act on alerts.
evidence: Antivirus status page; P07 SI-3 test

implementation_statement: No written supply chain process. POL-01 section 6 sets the sourcing rule, broker vetting, and receiving checks, scaled from NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1, by 2026-10-15.

In practice DoD orders are bought only from distributor A, an authorized source. Gap: the rule is not written, about 10% of commercial purchases come from a marketplace and brokers, and the owner's purchase orders do not carry the substance of FAR 52.204-25.

No anti-counterfeit procedure. OEM serial lookup is available through the partner portals but was never used on receipt. P07 testing found 2 cloned optic serials (2026-08-06). Receiving checks start by 2026-10-15 (POL-01 6.3).
evidence: P07 SR-11 results; OEM portal lookups
